 Vienna R1 previews and predictions: Tiafoe vs. Musetti, Nakashima vs. Griekspoor 
 October 27, 2026 
 Cheryl Murray 
 Match previews 
 1 
 Wednesday’s first-round matches in Vienna feature last week’s champions, with Lorenzo Musetti (Lyon) going up against Frances Tiafoe and Tallon Griekspoor (Brussels) taking on Brandon Nakashima. 
 Lorenzo Musetti vs. (6) Frances Tiafoe 
 The draw gods were not kind to No. 6 seed Frances Tiafoe. The American is clinging to a qualifying spot in the Nitto ATP Finals, and with Alex de Minaur, Novak Djokovic, and Taylor Fritz all chasing, he needs a good result in these last few tournaments. Lorenzo Musetti, meanwhile, walks in with a trophy. He won the Lyon title on Sunday, saving four match points against Flavio Cobolli in the semis before beating Taylor Fritz for his first title since 2022.
 Musetti has a good history in Vienna, reaching the semis in each of the last two years — and he is 5-0 indoors this season. The issue is the inevitable fatigue from the quick turnaround. Tiafoe leads the head-to-head 4-3 on the main tour (5-4 overall) and won their last meeting in the Cincinnati quarterfinals in August via a 7-6(2), 7-5 decision. I can see Musetti riding the Lyon momentum to a set, but I think Tiafoe’s power and fresher legs take over late. Look for Tiafoe to come through a tough one and protect his Turin spot.
 Cheryl pick: Tiafoe in 3 
 Ricky pick: Tiafoe in 2

 2 
 Brandon Nakashima vs. Tallon Griekspoor 
 This is a rematch of last year’s second round in Vienna, where Tallon Griekspoor beat Brandon Nakashima in a pair of tiebreakers. Griekspoor arrives in suddenly hot form. He triumphed in Brussels this past weekend for his fourth career title and his first since Mallorca in 2025. The Dutchman is up 10 spots to No. 50 in the world thanks to his recent victory.
 Andrew Patron/Delray Beach Open 
Nakashima, ranked 17th, has quietly put together one of his best seasons — with semifinal runs in Brisbane, Montreal and Cincinnati. He lost a tight three-setter to Cobolli in the quarters of Lyon, but he has generally been in good form. Like Musetti, the big question for Griekspoor is how much he has left in the tank. Four of his five matches in Brussels went the distance. Nakashima’s clean, steady baseline game is exactly the type that punishes tired legs. With Alexander Zverev waiting in the second round, the American also has plenty of reason to keep this one short. I think the Brussels hangover catches up with Griekspoor.
 Cheryl pick: Nakashima in 2 
 Ricky pick: Nakashima in 2
